invariants: The project repository owns current planning, design, structured data, approved runtime assets, code, scenes, resources, tests, and validation evidence for its domains.
ChatGPT Work is an execution surface and ChatGPT Library is reference storage; neither replaces repository paths, diffs, commits, or exact SHA authority.
The human-facing GDD PDF is a derived snapshot and must identify the exact source commit and evidence ceiling; editing the PDF alone does not change canon.
AI and Codex continuity is carried by repository Markdown, JSON, manifests, implementation files, tests, and handoffs rather than chat history or memory.
New Notion writes are not required by default. Existing Notion content may be read only to discover and migrate unique project information.
A project remains in LEGACY_READ_ONLY migration state until all three migration exit counters are zero and readback evidence is recorded.
Codex rehydrates the current project at an exact repository SHA before product mutation and does not assume chat or PDF state is newer than the repository.
An approved visual consumed by the product resolves to a project-controlled repository path, SHA-256 value, actual consumer, approval state, implementation state, and provenance record.
A generated or uploaded visual is not implementation-ready merely because it appears in chat, Library, a PDF, or a preview; the approved binary and manifest readback are required.
Human PDF review, document generation, static tests, and repository write success are distinct from runtime PASS, UX PASS, player PASS, and release PASS.
Notion retirement does not require destructive deletion. Historical workspaces may remain read-only for audit and rollback.
A project-specific Notion exception requires explicit user approval, a recorded scope and owner, a measurable value unavailable from the repository-first path, and an exit or revisit condition.
Google Sheets, Figma, HTML dashboards, ChatGPT Work, ChatGPT Library, and legacy Notion pages are not parallel project canon unless an explicit project-specific contract says otherwise.
